newsitem.title: USA: Lynch sees comparable Q3 results.
newsitem.headline: Lynch sees comparable Q3 results.

text.p: Lynch Corp said Monday that it expects comparisons for its third quarter to be similarly favorable to the 1996 third quarter.
"We expect operating results to be up, as they were in the second quarter to second quarter," said corporate secretary Robert Hurwich.

Earlier in the day the company reported a second quarter operating profit of $0.77 a share, compared to $0.58 in the year-ago quarter. Net profits were $0.88 a share, down from $1.77 in the 1996 quarter.

The company said it is continuing to examine the proposed split up of itself into its communications and manufacturing components, and that it is considering various strategic and/or financing options for each of its manufacturing units.

Spinnaker Industries is exploring various alternatives to pursue raising capital, including a secondary offering. Lynch Display Technologies, the newly created parent of Lynch Machinery, has started searching for horizontal/vertical acquisitions and is in discussions with various sources of financing.
Lynch said also that its M-tron unit is looking to make an acquisition/joint venture with a strategic partner.
"Success with any of these activities would be material to Lynch," a company statement said.
Lynch said its subsidiaries expect to make about $19 million of capital expenditures in 1997, down 25 percent from the $25.5 million in 1996.
It said 1998 capital spending should about equal capital spending in 1997, and that it expects depreciation to rise to $17.3 million in 1997 from $14.2 million in 1996.
